lines.text: Here's my take, and I've given it to every time-traveler who ever called: the theory earns its keep. It explains the human resemblance, the languages they seem to know, why people get taken and put back. Vallée spent fifty years arguing the phenomenon behaves like a thermostat for belief - keeping it at a set temperature. But here's the honest cost: it trades one impossible engine for another. Interstellar travel is hard physics. Time travel is harder physics. And neither one explains the radar tracks - a thing that fools two radars isn't running on belief alone.
